At the start of the first normal elongation cycle, where is the initiator tRNA?
A site|P site|E site|Outside the ribosome
Initiation places the first residue in P. The A site presents the next sense codon; E is associated with a departing spent tRNA.
Which bacterial factor normally delivers most elongator aminoacyl-tRNAs?
EF-Tu–GTP binds charged elongator tRNA. IF2 is an initiation factor, EF-G facilitates movement and EF-Ts exchanges nucleotide on EF-Tu.
What is the principal function of EF-Ts?
Phosphorylate GDP|Accelerate guanine nucleotide exchange on EF-Tu|Catalyze peptide hydrolysis|Bind the stop codon
EF-Ts promotes release of bound GDP; GTP then binds from the nucleotide pool. It is not a kinase or release factor.
The eukaryotic cytosolic counterpart of bacterial EF-G is:
eEF2 promotes translocation. eEF1A delivers charged tRNA, eEF1B supports exchange, and eIF2 participates in initiation.
Which group attacks the donor ester during ordinary peptide transfer?
P-site tRNA anticodon|A-site amino acid α-amino group|A-site amino acid carboxylate|GTP phosphate
The incoming amino group is the nucleophile; the donor is the ester carbonyl of the P-site peptidyl-tRNA. The incoming carboxyl linkage is retained.
Immediately after peptide transfer but before complete translocation, the elongated peptide is attached to which adaptor?
Original P-site tRNA|Original A-site tRNA|Free E-site tRNA|mRNA
The old chain is transferred onto the incoming residue. Its own tRNA retains the new C-terminal ester linkage; the former P tRNA is deacylated.
What is the net movement of a ribosome along a standard mRNA during one ordinary translocation?
One nucleotide toward 5′|Three nucleotides toward 3′|One amino acid toward 5′|Three codons toward 3′
The ribosome reads 5′ to 3′ and advances one triplet, not three triplets. Protein polarity is a separate description.
In a bacterial ribosome, which RNA forms the core peptidyl-transferase environment?
The catalytic center is in the large subunit and is formed principally by 23S rRNA. 16S rRNA contributes to small-subunit decoding.
Which statement about GTP in the standard cycle is correct?
It directly donates the amide nitrogen|It is consumed in factor cycles for delivery and movement|It is attached to every finished residue|Only EF-Ts hydrolyzes it
GTP supports conformational and kinetic steps. The activated donor ester supplies the chemically activated acyl group; GTP is not incorporated into peptide.
A tRNA has a correct anticodon but is charged with the wrong amino acid. What can happen?
It must be rejected by anticodon testing|A correct pairing can produce an incorrect amino acid sequence|It changes the mRNA sequence|It always terminates translation
The ribosome mainly tests pairing and geometry, not a complete amino-acid identity code. Upstream synthetase fidelity is therefore essential.
What does the A/P hybrid state mean?
Amino acid at P, anticodon outside|Anticodon region at small-subunit A and acceptor end at large-subunit P|Two different tRNAs share one anticodon|A tRNA carries two independent peptides
The slash notation separates the contacts of the two tRNA ends. Hybrid states are intermediates in movement, not additional independent tRNA species.
Which event is normally excluded from an ordinary elongation round?
GTP-dependent delivery|Peptide transfer|Translocation|Release-factor recognition of a stop codon
Release-factor action belongs to termination. The other three events constitute the repeating sense-codon cycle.
How many peptide bonds are present in an unmodified linear 12-residue peptide?
Each bond joins adjacent residues; 12 residues have 11 adjacent pairs. The first residue is present before the first elongation bond forms.
Aminoacylation normally consumes ATP to produce:
ADP only|AMP and pyrophosphate|GTP and AMP|Two ADP molecules
Activation passes through aminoacyl-AMP and releases PPi; transfer releases AMP. The conventional two-equivalent cost is not two ATP molecules directly consumed.

Attachment of free amino acid by a synthetase|Placement of the selected aminoacyl-tRNA acceptor end in the large-subunit reaction site|Removal of the start codon|Release of an entire completed protein
Accommodation is a ribosomal positioning step. Charging takes place before delivery; termination is a different reaction.
A near-cognate substrate is rejected after EF-Tu has hydrolyzed GTP. Which outcome follows?
The GTP is necessarily recovered intact|An energy cost can occur without an amino acid addition|A peptide bond necessarily forms|The mRNA is degraded immediately
A second discrimination step can reject the substrate after nucleotide hydrolysis. This accounts for excess GTP expenditure relative to product.
Which statement about normal wobble is most appropriate?
Every wobble pair is a decoding error|Permitted wobble allows some tRNAs to read multiple synonymous codons|Wobble always changes the frame|Wobble occurs in the peptide bond
Allowed pairing at the flexible codon position is part of normal decoding. Arbitrary mismatches are not all permitted.
What is the primary growth direction of a polypeptide?
C to N|N to C|3′ to 5′|Both ends equally
Incoming amino groups receive the pre-existing chain while their esterified carboxyl ends remain available for subsequent transfer.
Which factor is especially associated with efficient synthesis through difficult polyproline motifs in bacteria?
EF-P supports difficult peptide-transfer reactions. The other factors have initiation, termination or nucleotide exchange roles.
Why can a 30S and 50S subunit form a 70S ribosome?
10S is hydrolyzed|Sedimentation coefficients depend on hydrodynamic properties and are not additive|The A site removes mass|GTP changes the genetic code
Svedberg units measure sedimentation behavior rather than additive masses; association changes friction and shape.
Which result most directly reports covalent incorporation rather than substrate binding?
A labeled tRNA co-sediments with ribosome|Isolated peptide contains the labeled incoming amino acid|A tRNA anticodon pairs in solution|EF-Tu binds GTP
Purified peptide label establishes chemical transfer when free label and unreacted tRNA are excluded. Binding alone does not prove bond formation.
What is the role of the E site in ordinary elongation?
Recognize the next amino acid by charging it|Provide a route for departure of deacylated tRNA|Carry out ATP-to-AMP activation|Bind the initiation promoter
The spent adaptor moves toward E and leaves. It can subsequently be recharged outside the ribosome.
Which statement about an error-free peptide is correct?
It must always be folded and functional|It has the intended sequence, but folding can still fail|It necessarily contains no modifications|It requires no energy to synthesize
Sequence accuracy and biological activity are separate properties. Correctly encoded products can misfold or fail to mature.
Which statement best explains why the initial N-terminal portion can fold before translation ends?
The complete chain is synthesized at once|The chain emerges progressively as residues are added at C|The ribosome adds new residues to N|Every residue immediately leaves on its tRNA
N-terminal regions are synthesized earlier and can emerge while the C-terminal portion is still attached to a tRNA.
Assertion: A full-length protein can contain an incorrect residue. Reason: A missense decoding error need not alter the reading frame.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
An isolated substitution can leave frame and termination intact, allowing production of a full-length incorrect chain.
Assertion: Peptide transfer does not directly consume GTP as a chemical substrate. Reason: The donor peptide is attached to tRNA through an activated ester.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
The activated ester permits acyl transfer. GTP consumption at associated delivery and movement stages is mechanistically distinct.
Assertion: EF-Ts is a GTP-generating kinase. Reason: EF-Ts facilitates the removal of GDP from EF-Tu.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
GDP exchange is not phosphorylation. EF-Ts helps reset the binding state of EF-Tu.
Assertion: Hybrid tRNA states can arise after peptide transfer. Reason: Both tRNA ends must always move simultaneously.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
Hybrid states exist precisely because acceptor-end contacts can shift before complete anticodon-register movement.
Assertion: The ribosome can discriminate before and after delivery-associated GTP hydrolysis. Reason: Incorrect substrates may be rejected during accommodation.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
Post-hydrolysis rejection creates an additional decision point beyond initial selection.
Assertion: A synonymous substitution always increases translation speed. Reason: Different synonymous codons can be decoded by tRNAs with different cellular availabilities.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
Availability may differ, but the direction of a speed change depends on context. Synonymous is a code classification, not a universal kinetic prediction.
Which statements are correct? I. EF-Tu is involved in delivery. II. EF-G promotes translocation. III. EF-Ts directly adds phosphate to GDP.
I only|I and II|II and III|I, II and III
I and II describe the two elongation GTPases. III is incorrect because EF-Ts supports exchange rather than phosphorylation.
Match bacterial factor to function: 1 EF-Tu; 2 EF-Ts; 3 EF-G; a exchange; b delivery; c movement.
The mapping separates delivery from nucleotide exchange and movement.
I. GTP hydrolysis can occur before accommodation. II. Peptide transfer leaves the old P-site tRNA deacylated. III. The next codon is exposed by translocation. Which are correct?
I only|I and II|II and III|I, II and III
All three statements describe successive events of the canonical cycle.
Match eukaryotic factor to bacterial functional counterpart: 1 eEF1A; 2 eEF1B; 3 eEF2; a EF-G; b EF-Tu; c EF-Ts.
The counterparts are delivery, exchange and translocation, respectively.
I. Stop codons contribute no ordinary residue. II. A protein of n residues has n−1 peptide bonds. III. Every residue must enter via elongation-factor delivery.
I and III|II and III|I and II|All three
The initiator residue enters by initiation rather than ordinary A-site delivery. I and II are correct under standard uninterrupted translation.
A protein has 181 residues; all tRNAs are precharged and initiation is complete. Count GTP turnovers for ideal elongation up to presentation of stop.
There are 180 additions and 180 movements. Each uses one delivery GTP plus one movement GTP: 2 × 180 = 360. Charging and initiation are outside the boundary.
For 75 residues synthesized from free amino acids, excluding initiation, termination and recycling but including all charging, count high-energy phosphate equivalents.
Charging: 2 × 75 = 150; elongation: 2 × 74 = 148; total 298. The value 300 would add two unspecified equivalents.
A 501-residue protein has 500 elongation events, each with independent error probability 0.0002. Approximate chance of at least one error.
1−0.9998^500 ≈ 0.09517. The expected error number is 0.1, not exactly the probability of one or more errors.
Equal encounter frequencies: correct substrate passes first and second checks with conditional probabilities 0.8 and 0.9; wrong with 0.2 and 0.1. What fraction of products is wrong?
Correct weight = 0.72; wrong = 0.02; fraction 0.02/0.74 ≈ 2.70%. Do not use the first-stage error alone or the unnormalized 0.02.
Correct substrate arrives at relative rate 40 with acceptance 0.5; wrong arrives at 80 with acceptance 0.005. What is the wrong-product fraction?
Weights are 20 and 0.4. Error fraction 0.4/20.4 = 1.96%; the wrong/correct ratio is 2%, a different denominator.
A two-exit intermediate has forward rate 30 s⁻¹ and rejection rate 70 s⁻¹. Which pair gives forward probability and mean exit time?
Total exit rate is 100 s⁻¹; forward probability 30/100; mean wait 1/100 s. Both competing exits determine lifetime.
An elongation round has mean sequential times 25, 5 and 20 ms. Delivery time doubles; what is the new rate?
New cycle = 50+5+20 = 75 ms. Rate 1/0.075 = 13.33/s, not half the initial 20/s.
For 120 successful additions, mean delivery GTP use is 1.25 per addition and translocation costs one per addition. Find total expected elongation GTP.
Delivery 150 plus movement 120 gives 270. Extra GTP use arises from unsuccessful GTP-consuming delivery attempts.
A sequence has 80 additions at 0.04 s each and 20 at 0.12 s each. Determine elongation duration.
80×0.04 + 20×0.12 = 3.2 + 2.4 = 5.6 s. Sum durations, rather than averaging local rates.
A translated segment from AUG through the first in-frame stop contains 606 nt. With no recoding, how many elongation cycles occur?
606/3 = 202 codons including stop. There are 201 residues including initiator; therefore 200 ordinary cycles.
Two equal-concentration ligands differ in standard binding free energy by 5.7 kJ/mol in favor of the correct ligand. At 298 K with RT=2.48 kJ/mol, estimate wrong/correct equilibrium occupancy.
exp(−5.7/2.48) ≈ exp(−2.30) ≈ 0.10. It is an equilibrium occupancy ratio, not the final ribosomal error probability.
A mutant gives 92% normal dipeptide but only 5% normal downstream toeprint movement. Which stage is most directly implicated?
Covalent product can form while register change fails. The result supports a movement defect but does not alone identify a particular mutant protein.
A reaction produces no dipeptide and little bound incoming tRNA, although the initiator complex is normal. Adding EF-Tu restores both. What is best supported?
Primary delivery defect|Primary termination defect|Defective stop recognition|Proof that all tRNAs were mischarged
Rescue by delivery factor and low binding support a delivery problem; termination lies later. This does not establish the charging status of every tRNA.
A ribosome mutant produces more GTP hydrolysis but less correct product in a cognate/near-cognate mixture. Which additional measurement best separates rejection from uncoupled hydrolysis?
Total mRNA amount only|Number and identity of accommodated tRNAs, with background GTPase controls|Genomic DNA length|Final protein color alone
The state and identity of tRNAs after hydrolysis test passage through accommodation; factor-only and no-tRNA controls identify background turnover.
A cognate tRNA carrying an incorrect amino acid is accepted; a correctly charged near-cognate tRNA is usually rejected. What inference follows?
Codon testing alone proves correct charging|Charging fidelity and decoding fidelity are separable|All near-cognates always pass|Amino acids base-pair directly with mRNA
The two substrate types distinguish anticodon pairing from amino acid assignment. The ribosome is not a comprehensive synthetase identity checker.
A mutation reduces EF-Ts function. Active EF-Tu–GTP is initially abundant. Which time course is plausible?
Normal initial rounds followed by slowdown as EF-Tu–GDP accumulates|Immediate removal of all mRNA|More peptide bonds than residues|Termination at every first codon
Pre-existing active factor can support early cycles. Impaired exchange progressively reduces the delivery-competent pool; the other outcomes are not mechanistically implied.
The normal message AUG GCU UUU GGA UAA is translated. A movement inhibitor arrests the complex immediately after alanine incorporation. Which tRNA carries the chain before complete translocation?
Initiator tRNA at P|Alanine tRNA originally at A|Phenylalanine tRNA at E|Glycine tRNA at P
Transfer forms the Met–Ala chain on alanine tRNA. Phenylalanine is not yet added; the former initiator is deacylated.
A synonymous substitution causes slower synthesis at a specific codon; the transcript level is unchanged. Which experiment best evaluates a charged-tRNA supply explanation?

Measure charging fraction of relevant tRNA species and test rescue by adequate cognate substrate in a defined system|Count all genomic genes|Measure total ribosomal RNA only|Replace the stop codon with a promoter
Charged cognate supply directly affects productive arrival. RNA abundance and global ribosome counts alone cannot distinguish this specific cause.
Two hypothetical products have equal full-length yield, but one shows reduced enzyme activity. What is required to support a decoding-error explanation?
Only total full-length yield|Direct sequence-sensitive product analysis with appropriate folding controls|Only mRNA size|Only ATP concentration
Activity can change through misfolding or modification despite correct sequence; sequence-sensitive evidence plus controls is needed.
A chemical protection experiment shows A-site acceptor end has moved to large-subunit P but the anticodon remains at small-subunit A. Which interpretation is best?
Completed classical P/P state|A/P hybrid state|E/E exit state|Free tRNA charging
The contact pattern is the definition of A/P. The anticodon register has not completed the shift, so it is not P/P.
